quals-wisconsin-algebra-1997s-01.prompt:
Let $G$ be a finite group having the property that for every choice of two subgroups $X\subseteq G$ and $Y\subseteq G$, either $X\cap Y=1$ or $X\subseteq Y$ or $Y\subseteq X$.

(i) If $H\subseteq G$, show that either $|H|$ is a prime power or else that $|H|$ and $|G:H|$ are relatively prime.

(ii) If $1<N\trianglelefteq G$, prove that $G/N$ is nilpotent.

(iii) If $N\trianglelefteq G$ and $N\neq G$, show that $N$ is nilpotent.
quals-wisconsin-algebra-1997s-01.answer:
(i) If $|H|$ is not a prime power, each Sylow $p$-subgroup $P$ of $G$ meeting $H$ in a Sylow subgroup $
e1$ of $H$ must lie in $H$. (ii) Two Sylow subgroups $P/N,Q/N$ for different primes would give incomparable $P,Q$ with $P\cap Q=N
e1$; so $G/N$ is a $p$-group. (iii) For $1
e P\in\mathrm{Syl}_p(N)$, Frattini gives $G=NN_G(P)$, and $N_G(P)\cap N
e1$ forces $N\subseteq N_G(P)$, so every Sylow subgroup of $N$ is normal.

quals-wisconsin-algebra-1997s-02.prompt: Let $R$ be a ring, let $V$ be a right $R$-module, and suppose that $V=V_1\dotplus V_2\dotplus V_3\dotplus\cdots$ is the (internal) direct sum of its submodules $V_1,V_2,V_3,\ldots$. Show that $V$ is an Artinian module if and only if each $V_i$ is Artinian and only finitely many of the $V_i$'s are nonzero.
quals-wisconsin-algebra-1997s-02.answer: ($\Rightarrow$) Submodules of Artinian modules are Artinian, and the chain $W_i=V_i\dotplus V_{i+1}\dotplus\cdots$ stabilizes, forcing $V_i=0$ for large $i$. ($\Leftarrow$) Induction on the number of nonzero summands, using that an extension of an Artinian module by an Artinian module is Artinian.

quals-wisconsin-algebra-1997s-03.prompt:
Let $f(x)\in\mathbb{Q}[x]$ be a polynomial of degree $5$ over the rational numbers $\mathbb{Q}$ that is not solvable by radicals, and let $S$ be the splitting field of $f(x)$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ which is contained in the complex numbers.

(i) Show that there exists at most one subfield $E$ of $S$ such that $|E:\mathbb{Q}|=2$.

(ii) If $\alpha,\beta\in S$ are irrational elements which satisfy $\alpha^2\in\mathbb{Q}$ and $\beta^2\in\mathbb{Q}$, prove that $\alpha\beta\in\mathbb{Q}$.
quals-wisconsin-algebra-1997s-03.answer: (i) $G=\mathrm{Gal}(S/\mathbb{Q})$ is a nonsolvable subgroup of $S_5$, hence $A_5$ or $S_5$, which have $0$ resp. $1$ subgroups of index 2. (ii) Then $\mathbb{Q}[\alpha]=\mathbb{Q}[\beta]$, so $\beta=a\alpha+b$; squaring forces $b=0$, so $\alpha\beta=a\alpha^2\in\mathbb{Q}$.

quals-wisconsin-algebra-1997s-04.prompt:
If $K$ is a field, then the general linear group $G=GL_n(K)$ is the multiplicative group of $n\times n$ invertible matrices over $K$.

(i) If the characteristic of $K$ is not equal to $2$, show that $G$ has precisely $n$ conjugacy classes of elements of order $2$.

(ii) If $\mathrm{char}\,K=2$, show that $G$ has precisely $[n/2]$ (the greatest integer in $n/2$) conjugacy classes of elements of order $2$.
quals-wisconsin-algebra-1997s-04.answer: Conjugacy in $GL_n(K)$ is similarity. (i) $X^2=I$ with $x^2-1$ separable: $X\sim\mathrm{diag}(-I_r,I_{n-r})$, $1\le r\le n$, distinguished by $r=\mathrm{rank}(I-X)$. (ii) $(X-I)^2=0$: Jordan form with $r$ blocks $\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$, $1\le r\le\lfloor n/2\rfloor$, again $r=\mathrm{rank}(I-X)$.

quals-wisconsin-algebra-1997s-05.prompt: Let $S$ be a commutative integral domain and let $R$ be a subring of $S$ with the same identity $1$. Suppose that there exist finitely many elements $s_1,s_2,\ldots,s_n\in S$ such that $S=s_1R+s_2R+\cdots+s_nR$. Show that $R$ is a field if and only if $S$ is a field.
quals-wisconsin-algebra-1997s-05.answer: $S$ is a finitely generated $R$-module, hence integral over $R$. If $R$ is a field, multiplication by $s\ne0$ is an injective $R$-linear map of the finite-dimensional space $S$, hence surjective. If $S$ is a field and $0\ne r\in R$, an integral equation for $r^{-1}$ multiplied by $r^{n-1}$ shows $r^{-1}\in R$.
